name: Hip hop fashion

card.summary: A clothing and accessory style from hip-hop culture, from sportswear and gold chains to streetwear and luxury labels, used to shape a distinct personal look.

quick.overview:
Hip hop fashion is the dress style that grew out of hip-hop culture from the late 1970s, mixing sportswear, work wear, jewelry, sneakers and later luxury and designer labels.

People adopt it to build a recognisable look through silhouette, branded pieces, accessories and sneakers.
quick.how: People assemble outfits from items such as tracksuits, jerseys, baggy or oversized cuts, caps, sneakers and jewelry, often following current artists. Trends cycle between eras.
quick.risks: Some pieces are expensive, and critics including Chuck D argued that costly styles pressured low-income youth. Oral jewelry such as grills is noted in dental literature to favour plaque accumulation.

lead: Hip hop fashion emerged from urban Black American and inner-city youth culture in cities such as New York, Los Angeles and Atlanta, and spread widely across the United States.[1] In the late 1970s sportswear brands including Adidas, Kangol and Pro-Keds became attached to the scene.[1]

Its look has changed repeatedly: customised luxury logos by Dapper Dan in the early 1980s, Starter jackets and Dickies in West Coast style, FUBU and Sean John in the 1990s, and designer labels such as Rick Owens and Saint Laurent in the 2010s.[1]

For people thinking about appearance, it is a way to build a look through clothing and accessories rather than the body. Research touching on it includes a focus-group study on body image that found hip-hop fashion's popularity shaped peer norms among urban teenagers.[2]

angle.text: Clothing and accessories change how a person's frame and style read. People use hip hop fashion to project a particular identity and presence.

infobox: Late 1970s, US urban Black and Latino youth culture
Tracksuits, sneakers, jerseys, gold chains, grills

paras: Early DJs wore tracksuits, bomber jackets and sneakers from Adidas and Pro-Keds. Dapper Dan began customising luxury logos onto garments in the early 1980s, and performers popularised gold chains and large earrings.[1] Run-DMC's "My Adidas" came in 1986.[1]

In the 1990s labels such as Karl Kani, FUBU, Rocawear and Sean John expanded the market, and throwback jerseys, platinum and grills became common.[1] From around 2012, high-fashion labels became prominent among artists like A$AP Rocky and Travis Scott.[1]

Chuck D and others criticised the cost of hip-hop fashion for low-income youth, and several artists rejected expensive jewelry.[1] Some artists have used the style to challenge gender norms.[1] Tooth grills are described as status symbols in dental literature, which also notes they favour plaque accumulation and can affect articulation.[3]
No studies found. A focus-group study of African-American and Latino teenagers reported that hip-hop fashion's popularity contributed to peer norms about body image.[2]

timeline.event: Dapper Dan customises luxury logos onto clothing.[1]
Designer labels become prominent among artists such as A$AP Rocky.[1]
